pr_title: modem: iface_uart: disable TX interrupt when done
pr_body:
Disable the TX interrupt when the transmission completes. This stops
the nrf UARTE peripheral locking up the CPU with an interrupt storm.

Fixes #40371.

Signed-off-by: Jordan Yates <jordan.yates@data61.csiro.au>
pr_comments: Closing this as I am unable to reproduce the original issue on the latest versions of Zephyr

review_comments: The TX interrupt does not seem to be enabled by this driver (it sends data using `uart_poll_out`), so I don't entirely understand how is this supposed to help. What am I missing here?
Is there a chance that the Nordic UARTE driver has a bug that triggers the TX interrupt even when not using interrupt-driven transmission?

That was my initial thought, but I couldn't find in the UARTE driver code anything suspicious in this regard, hence I added my above comment. Now I additionally made a simple test application to check the driver behavior and it seems to work fine with RX using interrupts and TX only calling `uart_poll_out`.

We use the HL7800 modem driver on our product with an NRF52840 and do not see any issues like this.
The HL7800 uses `modem_recevier.c` and `mdm_receiver_setup` disables the TX interrupt before any other functions get used. This could be why it works ok in our case.
Could it be that `CONFIG_UART_<n>_ENHANCED_POLL_OUT=n`? If this option is disable then there is TX interrupt on ENDTX event just to trigger STOPTX task.

I set up the hardware again and the `TXSTOPPED` interrupt is definitely being enabled through `uart_poll_out` in the UARTE driver.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/83939c267c1a4ffe2644a913da79b5409e114f81/drivers/serial/uart_nrfx_uarte.c#L1493
